01
Before the first verse · Vol. 4, p. 598

Opening of the surah

Vol. 4, p. 598
Surah al-Haqqah. Meccan; it has 52 verses [revealed after (Surah) al-Mulk]. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
سورة الحاقة مكية، وآياتها 52 [نزلت بعد الملك] بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ
02
Q 69:1–8 · Vol. 4, pp. 598–600

Verses 1 to 8

The verses as the commentary quotes them
In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The Inevitable Reality (1) What is the Inevitable Reality? (2) And what will make you know what the Inevitable Reality is? (3) Thamud and 'Ad denied the Striking Calamity (4) As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the Overwhelming Blast (5) And as for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind (6) He imposed it upon them for seven nights and eight days continuously, so you would see the people therein lying prostrate, as if they were trunks of hollow palm trees (7) Then do you see of them any remnant? (8)
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الْحَاقَّةُ (1) مَا الْحَاقَّةُ (2) وَما أَدْراكَ مَا الْحَاقَّةُ (3) كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ وَعادٌ بِالْقارِعَةِ (4) فَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِالطَّاغِيَةِ (5) وَأَمَّا عادٌ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عاتِيَةٍ (6) سَخَّرَها عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيالٍ وَثَمانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُوماً فَتَرَى الْقَوْمَ فِيها صَرْعى كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجازُ نَخْلٍ خاوِيَةٍ (7) فَهَلْ تَرى لَهُمْ مِنْ باقِيَةٍ (8)
Vol. 4, p. 598
"Al-Haqqah" is the Hour whose occurrence is obligatory and whose coming is certain, which is coming with no doubt about it; or the one in which the "haqa'iq" (realities) of affairs — reckoning, reward and punishment — are found; or the one in which affairs are "made real" (tahiqqu), that is, are known in truth, from your saying "I do not know this (la ahiqqu hadha)," i.e., "I do not know its reality." The act (of "haqqa") is attributed to it, though it belongs to its people. Its nominative is as the subject, and its predicate is "What is the Inevitable Reality?" The original is: "al-haqqa, what is it?" — that is, "what thing is it?" — as a magnification of its matter and exaltation of its terror; so the explicit noun was put in place of the pronoun, because that is more terrifying for it. "And what will make you know": and what thing will make you know what the Inevitable Reality is — meaning: you have no knowledge of its essence or the extent of its greatness, since it is so great and severe that no one's understanding or imagination can reach it; and however you estimate its state, it is greater than that. "Ma" is in the nominative position as the subject. And "adraka" is suspended from it (ta'liq) because it contains the meaning of a question. "The Striking Calamity" (al-qari'a): that which strikes (taqra'u) people with terrors and horrors, the sky with splitting and rending, the earth and mountains with crushing and blasting, and the stars with obliteration and scattering. It was put in place of the pronoun to indicate the meaning of striking. In "al-haqqa" is an increase in describing its severity. When He mentioned it and magnified it, He followed that with mention of those who denied it and what befell them because of the denial, as a reminder to the people of Mecca and a warning to them of the consequence of their denial. "The Overwhelming Blast" (al-taghiya): the occurrence that exceeded the limit in severity. There is disagreement about it,
الْحَاقَّةُ الساعة الواجبة الوقوع الثابتة المجيء، التي هي آتية لا ريب فيها. أو التي فيها حواق الأمور من الحساب والثواب والعقاب. أو التي تحق فيها الأمور، أى: تعرف على الحقيقة، من قولك لا أحق هذا، أى: لا أعرف حقيقته. جعل الفعل لها وهو لأهلها وارتفاعها على الابتداء وخبرها مَا الْحَاقَّةُ والأصل: الحاقة ما هي، أى أىّ شيء هي تفخيما لشأنها وتعظيما لهو لها، فوضع الظاهر موضع المضمر، لأنه أهول لها وَما أَدْراكَ وأىّ شيء أعلمك ما الحاقة، يعنى: أنك لا علم لك بكنهها ومدى عظمها، على أنه من العظم والشدة بحيث لا يبلغه دراية أحد ولا وهمه، وكيفما قدرت حالها فهي أعظم من ذلك، وما في موضع الرفع على الابتداء. وأَدْراكَ معلق عنه لتضمنه معنى الاستفهام. بِالْقارِعَةِ التي تقرع الناس بالأفزاع والأهوال، والسماء بالانشقاق والانفطار، والأرض والجبال بالدك والنسف، والنجوم بالطمس والانكدار. ووضعت موضع الضمير لتدل على معنى القرع. في الحاقة: زيادة في وصف شدتها، ولما ذكرها وفخمها أتبع ذكر ذلك ذكر من كذب بها وما حل بهم بسبب التكذيب، تذكيرا لأهل مكة وتخويفا لهم من عاقبة تكذيبهم بِالطَّاغِيَةِ بالواقعة المجاوزة للحد في الشدة. واختلف فيها،
Vol. 4, p. 599
so it is said: the earthquake (rajfa). From Ibn 'Abbas: the thunderbolt (sa'iqa). From Qatada: God sent against them a cry (sayha) which silenced them. It is also said that "al-taghiya" is a verbal noun like "al-'afiya," i.e., "by their transgression (tughyan)," but it is not so, for lack of correspondence between it and His words "by a furious, violent wind." "Sarsar": the one with a loud sound, having a roaring (sarsara). It is also said: the cold one, from "sirr" (cold), as if it were the one in which cold was repeated and multiplied, so it burns by the intensity of its cold. "'Atiya": violent in blowing, and "'utuw" (defiance) is a metaphor; or it defied 'Ad, so they were unable to repel it by any stratagem — by taking cover in a building, or sheltering at a mountain, or hiding in a pit — for it would pull them out of their hiding places and destroy them. It is also said: it defied its keepers, so it came out with no measure or weight. It is narrated from the Messenger of God ﷺ: "God has not sent a ship's worth of wind except by measure, nor a drop of rain except by measure, save on the day of 'Ad and the day of Noah; for the water on the day of Noah overbore its keepers so they had no way (to control) it" — then he recited: "Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing ship" — "and the wind on the day of 'Ad defied its keepers so they had no way (to control) it" — then he recited: "by a furious, violent wind" [1]. Perhaps this is an expression for severity and excess therein. "Husum": it must be either the plural of "hasim" like "shuhud" and "qu'ud," or a verbal noun like "shukur" and "kufur." If it is a plural, then the meaning of "husuman" is ill-omened (days), which cut off (hasamat) all good and uprooted all blessing; or (days) in which the blowing of winds was continuous: it did not subside for an hour until it came upon them, a representation of its continuity by the continuity of the act of the cauterizer in repeating the cauterization on the sickness, time after time, until it is stopped (yanhasimu). If it is a verbal noun, then it is either put in the accusative by an implied verb, i.e., "tahsimu husuman," meaning "it uproots uprootingly"; or it is an attribute, as in your saying "possessed of cutting-off (dhat husum)"; or it is an object of purpose, i.e., "He imposed it upon them for uprooting." 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Zurara al-Kilabi said: "So time separated between their between, in which successive years of cutting-off followed one another" [2]. Al-Suddi read "husuman" with fatha, as a circumstantial clause from the wind, i.e., "He imposed it upon them uprooting." It is also said: they are the "days of the old woman" (ayyam al-'ajuz), which is because an old woman of 'Ad hid in a burrow, and the wind pulled her out on the eighth day and destroyed her. It is also said: they are the days of "al-'ajz" (the end), which are the last of winter, and its names are: al-sinn, al-sinnabr, al-wabr, and al-amir,
فقيل: الرجفة. وعن ابن عباس: الصاعقة. وعن قتادة: بعث الله عليهم صيحة فأهمدتهم. وقيل: الطاغية مصدر كالعافية، أى: بطغيانهم، وليس بذاك لعدم الطباق بينها وبين قوله بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ والصرصر: الشديدة الصوت لها صرصرة. وقيل: الباردة من الصر، كأنها التي كرر فيها البرد وكثر: فهي تحرق لشدة بردها عاتِيَةٍ شديدة العصف والعتوّ استعارة. أو عتت على عاد، فما قدروا على ردّها بحيلة، من استتار ببناء، أو لياذ بجبل، أو اختفاء في حفرة، فإنها كانت تنزعهم من مكامنهم وتهلكهم. وقيل: عتت على خزانها، فخرجت بلا كيل ولا وزن: وروى عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ما أرسل الله سفينة من ريح إلا بمكيال ولا قطرة من مطر إلا بمكيال إلا يوم عاد ويوم نوح، فإنّ الماء يوم نوح طغى على الخزان فلم يكن لهم عليه السبيل، ثم قرأ إِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَى الْماءُ حَمَلْناكُمْ فِي الْجارِيَةِ وإن الريح يوم عاد عتت على الخزان فلم يكن لهم عليها سبيل ثم قرأ بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عاتِيَةٍ «1» ولعلها عبارة عن الشدة والإفراط فيها. الحسوم: لا يخلو من أن يكون جمع حاسم كشهود وقعود. أو مصدرا كالشكور والكفور، فإن كان جمعا فمعنى قوله حُسُوماً نحسات حسمت كل خير واستأصلت كل بركة. أو متتابعة هبوب الرياح: ما خفتت ساعة حتى أتت عليهم تمثيلا لتتابعها بتتابع فعل الحاسم في إعادة الكي على الداء، كرة بعد أخرى حتى ينحسم. وإن كان مصدرا: فإما أن ينتصب بفعله مضمرا، أى: تحسم حسوما، بمعنى تستأصل استئصالا. أو يكون صفة كقولك: ذات حسوم. أو يكون مفعولا له، أى: سخرها عليهم للاستئصال. وقال عبد العزيز ابن زرارة الكلابي: ففرّق بين بينهم زمان … تتابع فيه أعوام حسوم «2» وقرأ السدى: حسوما، بالفتح حالا من الريح، أى: سخرها عليهم مستأصلة. وقيل: هي أيام العجوز، وذلك أن عجوزا من عاد توارت في سرب، فانتزعتها الريح في اليوم الثامن فأهلكتها. وقيل: هي أيام العجز، وهي آخر الشتاء وأسماؤها: الصن والصنبر، والوبر. والآمر،
Vol. 4, p. 600
al-mu'tamir, al-mu'allil, and the extinguisher of embers (mutfi' al-jamr). It is also said: "mukfi' al-za'n" [1]. The meaning of "He imposed it upon them": He gave it power over them as He willed "therein": in its blowing; or in the nights and days. And "a'jaz nakhil" has been read (with "nakhil"). "Of any remnant (baqiya)": of any remainder (baqiyya), or of any soul that remains, or of any remaining (baqa'), like "al-taghiya" in the sense of transgression.
والمؤتمر، والمعلل، ومطفئ الجمر. وقيل: مكفئ الظعن «1» ومعنى سَخَّرَها عَلَيْهِمْ سلطها عليهم كما شاء فِيها في مهابها. أو في الليالي والأيام. وقرئ: أعجاز نخيل مِنْ باقِيَةٍ من بقية أو من نفس باقية. أو من بقاء، كالطاغية: بمعنى الطغيان.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 599
1. (1) . Narrated by al-Tha'labi and Ibn Mardawayh from the narration of Musa ibn A'yan, from al-Thawri, from Musa ibn al-Musayyab, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn 'Abbas, raised to the Prophet. And narrated by al-Tabari by the route of Mihran ibn Abi 'Umar from Sufyan as a statement of (Ibn 'Abbas) only. [.....]
2. . By 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Zurara al-Kilabi. The original of the speech is "time separated between them (fa-farraqa baynahum zaman)," so "baynahum" is a locative of the separation; but he intended emphasis by making the separation also between the parts of this locative, so he said "farraqa bayna baynihim zaman"; and when the locative is separated, its companions are necessarily separated, so it falls under metonymy. It is possible that the second "bayn" is a metonymy for the link between them; perhaps its original is "farraqa bayna dhat baynihim," and he explained the cause of time's separating them by describing it as one in which successive years of "husum" followed one another — from "al-hasm": cutting, and cauterizing with fire time after time until the blood is cut off. The apparent meaning of al-Jawhari's words is that it is singular, for he said: "ayyam husum," i.e., uprooting. And "al-husum": ill-omen. It is also possible that it is the plural of "hasim," like "raki'" and "ruku'," "sajid" and "sujud," i.e., things that cut off and sever the doors of good things.
1. (1) . أخرجه الثعلبي وابن مردويه من رواية موسى بن أعين عن الثوري عن موسى بن المسيب عن شهر بن حوشب عن ابن عباس مرفوعا. وأخرجه الطبري من طريق مهران بن أبى عمر عن سفيان موقوفا. [.....]
2. . لعبد العزيز بن زرارة الكلابي، وأصل الكلام: ففرق بينهم زمان، فبينهم ظرف للتفريق، إلا أنه أراد المبالغة بجعل التفريق بين أجزاء هذا الظرف أيضا، فقال: ففرق بين بينهم زمان، وإذا فرق بين الظرف فقد فرق بين أصحابه بالضرورة، فهو من باب الكناية. ويمكن أن بين الثاني كناية عن الوصلة التي بينهم، ولعل أصله: ففرق بين ذات بينهم، وبين سبب تفريق الزمان بينهم بوصفه بأنه تتابع فيه أعوام حسوم، من الحسم: وهو القطع، والكي بالنار مرة بعد أخرى حتى ينقطع الدم. وظاهر كلام الجوهري أنه مفرد، لأنه قال: أيام حسوم، أى: مستأصلة. والحسوم: الشؤم. ويجوز أنه جمع حاسم كراكع وركوع، وساجد وسجود، أى: حاسمات وقاطعات لأبواب الخيرات.
Vol. 4, p. 600
1. (1) . His statement "and it is said mukfi' al-za'n": the plural of "za'ina," which is the howdah (hawdaj), as stated in al-Sihah. ('A)
2. . Mahmud (al-Zamakhshari) said: "It is said 'wa'aytuhu,' i.e., I preserved it in yourself … etc." Ahmad (Ibn al-Munir) said: It is like His words "and let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow" — and it has been mentioned that the benefit of indefiniteness and singularity there is to signal the fewness of those who look.
3. . Narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur and al-Tabari from the narration of Makhul with it, mursal, in full or similar. And al-Tha'labi narrated it by the route of Abu Hamza al-Thumali: 'Abd God ibn Hasan told me, saying: When it was revealed… — and he mentioned it in the wording of the author.
1. (1) . قوله «وقيل مكفئ الظعن» جمع ظعينة وهي الهودج، أفاده الصحاح. (ع)
2. . قال محمود: «يقال وعيته أى حفظته في نفسك
…. الخ» قال أحمد: هو مثل قوله وَلْتَنْظُرْ نَفْسٌ ما قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ وقد ذكر أن فائدة التنكير والتوحيد فيه الاشعار قلة الناظرين.
3. . أخرجه سعيد بن منصور والطبري من رواية مكحول به مرسلا بتمامه نحوه. وأخرجه الثعلبي من طريق أبى حمزة الثمالي حدثني عبد الله بن حسن قال: حين نزلت فذكره بلفظ المصنف.
03
Q 69:9–10 · Vol. 4, p. 600

Verses 9 to 10

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And Pharaoh and those before him and the overturned cities came with the sinful deed (9) And they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with an ever-increasing seizure (10)
وَجاءَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَنْ قَبْلَهُ وَالْمُؤْتَفِكاتُ بِالْخاطِئَةِ (9) فَعَصَوْا رَسُولَ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَخَذَهُمْ أَخْذَةً رابِيَةً (10)
Vol. 4, p. 600
"And those before him": he means those of his followers who were with him. It has also been read "wa-man qibalahu" (those who preceded him). The first is supported by the reading of 'Abd God and Ubayy: "and those with him," and the reading of Abu Musa: "and those in his presence." "The overturned cities" (al-mu'tafikat): the towns of the people of Lot. "With the sinful deed (al-khati'a)": with the error, or the act, or the acts of great error. "Rabiya": severe, increasing in severity, as their ugly deeds increased in ugliness. It is said "raba al-shay' yarbu" when it increases: "that it may increase in the wealth of people."
وَمَنْ قَبْلَهُ يريد: ومن عنده من تباعه. وقرئ: ومن قبله، أى: ومن تقدمه. وتعضد الأولى قراءة عبد الله وأبى: ومن معه. وقراءة أبى موسى: ومن تلقاءه وَالْمُؤْتَفِكاتُ قرى قوم لوط بِالْخاطِئَةِ بالخطإ، أو بالفعلة، أو الأفعال ذات الخطإ العظيم رابِيَةً شديدة زائدة في الشدة، كما زادت قبائحهم في القبح. يقال: ربا الشيء يربو: إذا زاد لِيَرْبُوَا فِي أَمْوالِ النَّاسِ.

Q 69:11–12 · Vol. 4, pp. 600–601

Verses 11 to 12

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing ship (11) That We might make it for you a reminder, and that a retaining ear might retain it (12)
إِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَى الْماءُ حَمَلْناكُمْ فِي الْجارِيَةِ (11) لِنَجْعَلَها لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَةً وَتَعِيَها أُذُنٌ واعِيَةٌ (12)
Vol. 4, p. 600
"We carried you": We carried your forefathers "in the sailing ship": in a vessel, because when they are descended from those carried and saved, the carrying of their forefathers is a favor upon them, as if they were the ones carried, since their rescue is the cause of their birth. "That We might make it": the pronoun refers to the deed — the rescue of the believers and the drowning of the disbelievers — "a reminder": an admonition and a lesson. "A retaining ear": one whose nature is to retain and preserve what it has heard and not lose it by neglecting to act; and everything you preserve in yourself you have "wa'aytahu" [2], and what you preserve in something other than yourself you have "aw'aytahu," as in your saying "wa'aytu al-shay' fi al-zarf" (I stored the thing in the container). It is related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said to 'Ali ؓ when this verse was revealed: "I asked God to make it your ear, O 'Ali." 'Ali ؓ said: "I have forgotten nothing since, and it was not for me to forget" [3].
حَمَلْناكُمْ حملنا آباءكم فِي الْجارِيَةِ في سفينة، لأنهم إذا كانوا من نسل المحمولين الناجين، كان حمل آبائهم منة عليهم، وكأنهم هم المحمولون، لأن نجاتهم سبب ولادتهم لِنَجْعَلَها الضمير للفعلة: وهي نجاة المؤمنين وإغراق الكفرة تَذْكِرَةً عظة وعبرة أُذُنٌ واعِيَةٌ من شأنها أن تعى وتحفظ ما سمعت به ولا تضيعه بترك العمل، وكل ما حفظته في نفسك فقد وعيته «2» وما حفظته في غير نفسك فقد أوعيته كقولك: وعيت الشيء في الظرف. وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال لعلىّ رضى الله عنه عند نزول هذه الآية «سألت الله أن يجعلها أذنك يا علىّ» قال علىّ رضى الله عنه: فما نسيت شيئا بعد وما كان لي أن أنسى «3» .
Question
If you ask: why was it said "an ear that retains" in the singular and indefinite?
فإن قلت: لم قيل: أذن واعية، على التوحيد والتنكير؟
Answer
I say: to signal that the retainers among them are few; to rebuke the people for the fewness of those among them who retain; and to indicate that a single ear that retains and understands from God is the greatest multitude before God, and that all others are not given the slightest regard, even if they fill what is between the two horizons. It has also been read "wa-ta'iyha" with sukun on the 'ayn for lightening, likening "ta'i" to "kabid.
قلت: للإيذان بأن الوعاة فيهم قلة، ولتوبيخ الناس بقلة من يعي منهم، وللدلالة على أن الأذن الواحدة إذا وعت وعقلت عن الله فهي السواد الأعظم عند الله، وأن ما سواها لا يبالى بهم بالة وإن ملئوا ما بين الخافقين. وقرئ: وتعيها بسكون العين للتخفيف: شبه تعى بكبد.
Vol. 4, p. 601
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 600
1. (1) . His statement "and it is said mukfi' al-za'n": the plural of "za'ina," which is the howdah (hawdaj), as stated in al-Sihah. ('A)
2. . Mahmud (al-Zamakhshari) said: "It is said 'wa'aytuhu,' i.e., I preserved it in yourself … etc." Ahmad (Ibn al-Munir) said: It is like His words "and let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow" — and it has been mentioned that the benefit of indefiniteness and singularity there is to signal the fewness of those who look.
3. . Narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur and al-Tabari from the narration of Makhul with it, mursal, in full or similar. And al-Tha'labi narrated it by the route of Abu Hamza al-Thumali: 'Abd God ibn Hasan told me, saying: When it was revealed… — and he mentioned it in the wording of the author.
1. (1) . قوله «وقيل مكفئ الظعن» جمع ظعينة وهي الهودج، أفاده الصحاح. (ع)
2. . قال محمود: «يقال وعيته أى حفظته في نفسك
…. الخ» قال أحمد: هو مثل قوله وَلْتَنْظُرْ نَفْسٌ ما قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ وقد ذكر أن فائدة التنكير والتوحيد فيه الاشعار قلة الناظرين.
3. . أخرجه سعيد بن منصور والطبري من رواية مكحول به مرسلا بتمامه نحوه. وأخرجه الثعلبي من طريق أبى حمزة الثمالي حدثني عبد الله بن حسن قال: حين نزلت فذكره بلفظ المصنف.

1. (1) . Mahmud said: "If you ask: why did He say 'one' when there are two blasts … etc."? Ahmad said: As for the benefit of signaling the greatness of this blast: that what effects the crushing of the earth and mountains and the ruin of the world is this one alone, needing no other.

Q 69:13–18 · Vol. 4, pp. 601–602

Verses 13 to 18

The verses as the commentary quotes them
So when the Horn is blown with one blast (13) And the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing (14) Then on that Day the Inevitable Event will occur (15) And the heaven will split open, for that Day it will be frail (16) And the angels will be on its edges; and above them, on that Day, eight will bear the Throne of your Lord (17) On that Day you will be exposed; no secret of yours will remain hidden (18)
فَإِذا نُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌ واحِدَةٌ (13) وَحُمِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ وَالْجِبالُ فَدُكَّتا دَكَّةً واحِدَةً (14) فَيَوْمَئِذٍ وَقَعَتِ الْواقِعَةُ (15) وَانْشَقَّتِ السَّماءُ فَهِيَ يَوْمَئِذٍ واهِيَةٌ (16) وَالْمَلَكُ عَلى أَرْجائِها وَيَحْمِلُ عَرْشَ رَبِّكَ فَوْقَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ ثَمانِيَةٌ (17) يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لا تَخْفى مِنْكُمْ خافِيَةٌ (18)
Vol. 4, p. 601
The verb is attributed to the verbal noun, and its being masculine is acceptable because of the separation. Abu al-Sammal read "nafkhatan wahidatan" with the accusative, attributing the verb to the prepositional phrase. If you ask: there are two blasts, so why was it said "one" [1]? I say: its meaning is that it is not repeated in its time. If you ask: which of the two blasts is it? I say: the first, because at it comes the corruption of the world; and so is the narration from Ibn 'Abbas. And it has also been narrated from him that it is the second. If you ask: did He not say afterward "On that Day you will be exposed," while exposure is only at the second blast? I say: He made "the Day" a name for the wide span of time in which occur the two blasts, the swoon, the resurrection, the standing and the reckoning; so it was said "On that Day you will be exposed," just as you say "I came to him in such-and-such a year," when your coming was only at one moment of its times. "And were lifted": and raised from their sides by a wind whose blowing reached such strength that it carries the earth and mountains; or by a creation of angels; or by the power of God without a cause. It has also been read "wa-hamalat" (with the omission of the carrier, which is one of the three). "And were crushed": the two masses were crushed — the mass of the lands and the mass of the mountains — striking against one another until they are pulverized and return as a heap of sliding sand and scattered dust. "Dakk" is more intense than "daqq." It is also said: "so they were spread out in one spreading," becoming a land in which you see no crookedness or unevenness, from your saying "indakka al-sanam" when the hump flattens; and a "ba'ir adakk" and a "naqa dakka'." From it comes "al-dukkan." "Then on that Day the Inevitable Event will occur": at that time the descending calamity — the Resurrection — will descend. "Frail" (wahiya): slack, its strength utterly fallen after having been firm and tightly held. He means: the creation that is called "the angel (malak)," and the pronoun returned to it in the plural in His words "above them" according to the sense. If you ask: what is the difference between His saying "the angel (al-malak)" and saying "the angels (al-mala'ika)"? I say: "al-malak" is more general than "al-mala'ika"; do you not see that your saying "there is no angel but he is a witness" is more general than your saying "there are no angels…" "On its edges": on its sides; the singular is "raja'," shortened — meaning: it splits, and it is the dwelling of the angels, so they gather [2] to its edges and the surroundings of its borders [3]. "Eight": that is, eight
أسند الفعل إلى المصدر، وحسن تذكيره للفصل. وقرأ أبو السمال نفخة واحدة بالنصب مسندا للفعل إلى الجار والمجرور. فإن قلت: هما نفختان، فلم قيل: واحدة «1» ؟ قلت معناه أنها لا تثنى في وقتها. فإن قلت: فأى النفختين هي؟ قلت الأولى لأن عندها فساد العالم، وهكذا الرواية عن ابن عباس. وقد روى عنه أنها الثانية. فإن قلت: أما قال بعد يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ والعرض إنما هو عند النفخة الثانية؟ قلت: جعل اليوم اسما للحين الواسع الذي تقع فيه النفختان والصعقة والنشور والوقوف والحساب، فلذلك قيل يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ كما تقول: جئته عام كذا، وإنما كان مجيئك في وقت واحد من أوقاته وَحُمِلَتِ ورفعت من جهاتها بريح بلغت من قوّة عصفها أنها تحمل الأرض والجبال. أو بخلق من الملائكة. أو بقدرة الله من غير سبب. وقرئ: وحملت، بحذف المحمل وهو أحد الثلاثة فَدُكَّتا فدكت الجملتان: جملة الأرضين وجملة الجبال، فضرب بعضها ببعض حتى تندقّ وترجع كثيبا مهيلا وهباء منبثا. والدك أبلغ من الدق. وقيل: فبسطتا بسطة واحدة، فصارتا أرضا لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا، من قولك: اندكّ السنام إذا انفرش. وبعير أدك وناقة دكاء. ومنه: الدكان فَيَوْمَئِذٍ وَقَعَتِ الْواقِعَةُ فحينئذ نزلت النازلة وهي القيامة واهِيَةٌ مسترخية ساقطة القوّة جدّا بعد ما كانت محكمة مستمسكة. يريد: والخلق الذي يقال له الملك، وردّ إليه الضمير مجموعا في قوله فَوْقَهُمْ على المعنى: فإن قلت: ما الفرق بين قوله وَالْمَلَكُ، وبين أن يقال والملائكة؟ قلت: الملك أعمّ من الملائكة، ألا ترى أن قولك: ما من ملك إلا وهو شاهد، أعم من قولك: ما من ملائكة عَلى أَرْجائِها على جوانبها: الواحد رجا مقصور، يعنى: أنها تنشق، وهي مسكن الملائكة، فينضوون «2» إلى أطرافها وما حولها من حافاتها «3» ثَمانِيَةٌ أى: ثمانية
Vol. 4, p. 602
of them. From the Messenger of God ﷺ: "Today they are four, and when it is the Day of Resurrection God will strengthen them with four others, so they will be eight" [1]. It is also narrated: eight angels, their feet at the bases of the seventh earth, the Throne above their heads, and they are bowed in glorification. It is said: some are in the form of a human, some in the form of a lion, some in the form of a bull, and some in the form of an eagle. It is also narrated: eight angels in the form of mountain goats, between their hooves and their knees is a journey of seventy years. From Shahr ibn Hawshab: four of them say: "Glory be to You, O God, and praise; to You is praise for Your pardon after Your power," and four say: "Glory be to You, O God, and praise; to You is praise for Your forbearance after Your knowledge." From al-Hasan: God knows how many they are — eight, or eight thousand? From al-Dahhak: eight ranks whose number only God knows. It is also possible that the eight are of the Spirit, or of another creation, for He is able to create anything: "Glory be to the One who created all the pairs from what the earth grows and from themselves and from what they do not know." "Exposure" (al-'ard): an expression for reckoning and questioning; it is likened to a ruler's reviewing his troops in order to learn their conditions. It is narrated that on the Day of Resurrection there are three exposures: as for two of them, they are excuse, argument and rebuke; as for the third, in it the records are spread out, so the successful takes his record in his right hand and the doomed takes his in his left. "Hidden thing" (khafiya): a secret and a condition that was concealed in the world by God's covering you.
منهم. وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «هم اليوم أربعة، فإذا كان يوم القيامة أيدهم الله بأربعة آخرين فيكونون ثمانية «1» » وروى: ثمانية أملاك: أرجلهم في تخوم الأرض السابعة، والعرش فوق رؤسهم، وهم مطرقون مسبحون. وقيل: بعضهم على صورة الإنسان، وبعضهم على صورة الأسد، وبعضهم على صورة الثور، وبعضهم على صورة النسر. وروى: ثمانية أملاك في خلق الأوعال، ما بين أظلافها إلى ركبها: مسيرة سبعين عاما. وعن شهر بن حوشب: أربعة منهم يقولون: سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك لك الحمد على عفوك بعد قدرتك، وأربعة يقولون: سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك، لك الحمد على حلمك بعد علمك. وعن الحسن: الله أعلم كم هم، أثمانية أم ثمانية آلاف؟ وعن الضحاك: ثمانية صفوف لا يعلم عددهم إلا الله. ويجوز أن تكون الثمانية من الروح، أو من خلق آخر، فهو القادر على كل خلق، سبحان الذي خلق الأزواج كلها مما تنبت الأرض ومن أنفسهم ومما لا يعلمون. العرض: عبارة عن المحاسبة والمساءلة. شبه ذلك بعرض السلطان العسكر لتعرف أحواله. وروى أنّ في يوم القيامة ثلاثة عرضات، فأما عرضتان فاعتذار واحتجاج وتوبيخ، وأما الثالثة ففيها تنشر الكتب فيأخذ الفائز كتابه بيمينه والهالك كتابه بشماله خافِيَةٌ سريرة وحال كانت تخفى في الدنيا بستر الله عليكم.

1. (1) . Narrated by al-Tabari by the route of Abu Ishaq, who said: It has reached us that the Messenger of God ﷺ said — and he mentioned it. It is mentioned in the long hadith narrated by Isma'il ibn Rafi' from Zayd ibn Abi Ziyad, from al-Qurazi, from a man, from Abu Hurayra. Narrated by Abu Ya'la and others, and it has preceded.

1. (1) . أخرجه الطبري من طريق أبى إسحاق. قال: بلغنا أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال- فذكره. وهو مذكور في الحديث الطويل الذي يرويه إسماعيل بن رافع عن زيد بن أبى زياد عن القرظي عن رجل عن أبى هريرة. رواه أبو يعلى وغيره وقد تقدم.
2. . قوله «كأف وحس، وما أشبه ذلك» يفهم من كل منهما معنى التضجر والتألم، كما يفيده الصحاح. (ع)
06
Q 69:19–24 · Vol. 4, pp. 602–603

Verses 19 to 24

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Then as for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: Here, read my record! (19) Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my account (20) So he will be in a pleasant life (21) In an elevated Garden (22) Its fruits are near at hand (23) Eat and drink in satisfaction for what you put forth in the days gone by (24)
فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَيَقُولُ هاؤُمُ اقْرَؤُا كِتابِيَهْ (19) إِنِّي ظَنَنْتُ أَنِّي مُلاقٍ حِسابِيَهْ (20) فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ (21) فِي جَنَّةٍ عالِيَةٍ (22) قُطُوفُها دانِيَةٌ (23) كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئاً بِما أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِي الْأَيَّامِ الْخالِيَةِ (24)
Vol. 4, p. 602
"As for" is the detailing of the exposure. "Ha": a sound that is uttered and from which the meaning "take" is understood, like "uff" and "hass" and the like [2]. And "kitabiyah" is in the accusative by "ha'um" according to the Kufans, and by "iqra'u" according to the Basrans, because it is the nearer of the two governors. Its original is: "ha'um kitabi, iqra'u kitabi," and the first was omitted because the second indicates it. Its like is "Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper." They said: had the governor been the first, it would have been said "iqra'uhu" and "afrighuhu." And the "ha" is the pausal ha' (ha' al-sakt) in "kitabiyah," and likewise in "hisabiyah," "maliyah" and "sultaniyah." And the right of these ha's is that they
فَأَمَّا تفصيل للعرض. ها: صوت يصوت به فيفهم منه معنى «خذ» كأف وحس، وما أشبه ذلك «2» . وكِتابِيَهْ منصوب بهاؤم عند الكوفيين، وعند البصريين باقرءوا، لأنه أقرب العاملين. وأصله: هاؤم كتابي اقرؤا كتابي، فحذف الأوّل لدلالة الثاني عليه. ونظيره آتُونِي أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْراً قالوا: ولو كان العامل الأوّل لقيل: اقرؤه وأفرغه. والهاء للسكت في كِتابِيَهْ، وكذلك في حِسابِيَهْ ومالِيَهْ وسُلْطانِيَهْ وحق هذه الهاءات أن
Vol. 4, p. 603
are retained in pause and dropped in continuation [1]; and it is recommended to prefer pausing, preferring their retention, since they are retained in the Mushaf. It is also said: there is no harm in continuing and dropping. Ibn Muhaysin read with sukun on the ya' without ha'. A group read with the ha' retained in both continuation and pause, following the Mushaf. "I was certain" (zanantu): I knew. Assumption (zann) was treated as knowledge only because strong assumption is put in the place of knowledge in customs and rulings. It is said: "I assume an assumption like certainty that the matter is such and such." "Pleasant" (radiya): attributed to pleasure (rida'), like "dari'" (armored) and "nabil" (having arrows). The attribution is of two kinds: attribution by a particle, and attribution by form. Or the act was given to it figuratively, while it belongs to its owner. "Elevated" ('aliya): high in place in the sky; or high in degrees; or high in buildings, palaces and trees. "Near at hand" (daniya): reached by the one sitting and the one lying down. It is said to them: "Eat and drink in satisfaction" [2] — eating and drinking that are wholesome — or "you have been given satisfaction" as a verbal noun. "For what you put forth": for the righteous deeds you advanced "in the days gone by": the past days of the world. From Mujahid: the days of fasting, i.e., eat and drink in exchange for what you withheld from eating and drinking for the sake of God. It is narrated: God, Mighty and Majestic, says: "O My friends, long did I look upon you in the world while your lips had shriveled from drinks, your eyes were sunken, and your bellies were empty; so be today in your bliss, and eat and drink in satisfaction for what you put forth in the days gone by."
تثبت في الوقف وتسقط في الوصل، «1» وقد استحب إيثار الوقف إيثارا لثباتها لثباتها في المصحف. وقيل: لا بأس بالوصل والإسقاط. وقرأ ابن محيصن بإسكان الياء بغير هاء. وقرأ جماعة بإثبات الهاء في الوصل والوقف جميعا لاتباع المصحف ظَنَنْتُ علمت. وإنما أجرى الظن مجرى العلم، لأن الظن الغالب يقام مقام العلم في العادات والأحكام. ويقال: أظن ظنا كاليقين أنّ الأمر كيت وكيت راضِيَةٍ منسوبة إلى الرضا، كالدارع والنابل. والنسبة نسبتان: نسبة بالحرف، ونسبة بالصيغة. أو جعل الفعل لها مجازا وهو لصاحبها عالِيَةٍ مرتفعة المكان في السماء. أو رفيعة الدرجات. أو رفيعة المبانى والقصور والأشجار دانِيَةٌ ينالها القاعد والنائم. يقال لهم كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئاً «2» أكلا وشربا هنيئا. أو هنيتم هنيئا على المصدر بِما أَسْلَفْتُمْ بما قدمتم من الأعمال الصالحة فِي الْأَيَّامِ الْخالِيَةِ الماضية من أيام الدنيا. وعن مجاهد: أيام الصيام، أى: كلوا واشربوا بدل ما أمسكتم عن الأكل والشرب لوجه الله. وروى. يقول الله عز وجل: يا أوليائى طالما نظرت إليكم في الدنيا وقد قلصت شفاهكم عن الأشربة، وغارت أعينكم، وخمصت بطونكم، فكونوا اليوم في نعيمكم، وكلوا واشربوا هنيئا بما أسلفتم في الأيام الخالية.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 602
1. (1) . Narrated by al-Tabari by the route of Abu Ishaq, who said: It has reached us that the Messenger of God ﷺ said — and he mentioned it. It is mentioned in the long hadith narrated by Isma'il ibn Rafi' from Zayd ibn Abi Ziyad, from al-Qurazi, from a man, from Abu Hurayra. Narrated by Abu Ya'la and others, and it has preceded.
2. . His statement "like uff and hass and the like": from each of them is understood the meaning of vexation and pain, as al-Sihah indicates. ('A)
1. (1) . أخرجه الطبري من طريق أبى إسحاق. قال: بلغنا أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال- فذكره. وهو مذكور في الحديث الطويل الذي يرويه إسماعيل بن رافع عن زيد بن أبى زياد عن القرظي عن رجل عن أبى هريرة. رواه أبو يعلى وغيره وقد تقدم.
2. . قوله «كأف وحس، وما أشبه ذلك» يفهم من كل منهما معنى التضجر والتألم، كما يفيده الصحاح. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 603
1. (1) . Mahmud said: "The right of these ha's — meaning in kitabiyah, hisabiyah, maliyah and sultaniyah … etc." Ahmad said: Explaining the reading by following the Mushaf is astonishing, given that the true belief is that the seven readings, with their details, are transmitted by mass-transmission (tawatur) from the Prophet, may God's blessings be upon him and his family. So the one who retained the ha' in continuation retained it only from the mass-transmitted recitation of the Prophet ﷺ: he recited it so before it was written in the Mushaf. What troubles these people is only introducing personal reasoning (ijtihad) into the widely-transmitted readings, and believing that among them are some taken by speculative choice; and this is an error whose door ought not to be opened, for it is a path to what is greater than it. There once took place between me and Shaykh Abu 'Amr ؒ a discussion about His words "And whoever obeys God and His Messenger and fears God and is mindful of Him" according to the reading of Hafs, which ended with his being bound to refute whoever retains the ha' in continuation in the words of Surah al-Haqqah; for I had argued against him with the retention of it by the famous reciters in just this way. From his rebuttal I understood what he understood from al-Zamakhshari's words here, and I did not accept it from him ؒ and he retracted it. That discussion was by correspondence between him and me, and it was the last thing he wrote on the sciences, as his close companions informed me; and that is sound, because it was in the early part of his illness ؒ. And God knows best.
2. . His statement "eat and drink in satisfaction": in al-Sihah: "hani'a al-ta'am" and "hani'a," i.e., became wholesome. "Hana'ani al-ta'am yahni'uni and yahna'uni," which has no parallel among hamzated verbs; "hana'" and "hina'." And "hani'tu al-ta'am," i.e., I enjoyed it; and "eat it wholesome and pleasant." ('A)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «وحق هذه الهاءات يعنى في كتابيه وحسابيه وماليه وسلطانيه
…. الخ» قال أحمد: تعليل القراءة باتباع المصحف عجيب مع أن المعتقد الحق أن القراآت السبع بتفاصيلها منقولة تواترا عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وعلى آله وسلم، فالذي أثبت الهاء في الوصل إنما أثبتها من التواتر عن قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: آيها كذلك قبل أن تكتب في المصحف، وما نفس هؤلاء إلا إدخال الاجتهاد في القراآت المستفيضة، واعتقاد أن فيها ما أخذ بالاختيار النظري وهذا خطأ لا ينبغي فتح بابه، فانه ذريعة إلى ما هو أكبر منه، ولقد جرت بيني وبين الشيخ أبى عمرو رحمه الله مفاوضة في قوله وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَيَخْشَ اللَّهَ وَيَتَّقْهِ على قراءة حفص، انتهت إلى أن ألزم الرد على من أثبت الهاء في الوصل في كلمات سورة الحاقة. لأنى حججته بإثبات القراء المشاهير لها كذلك، ففهمت من رده لذلك ما فهمه من كلام الزمخشري هاهنا ولم أقبله منه رحمه الله، فتراجع عنه، وكانت هذه المفاوضة بمكاتبة بيني وبينه، وهي آخر ما كتب من العلوم على ما أخبرنى به خاصته، وذلك صحيح لأنها كانت في أوائل مرضه رحمه الله، والله أعلم.
2. . قوله «كلوا واشربوا هنيئا» في الصحاح: هنؤ الطعام وهنيء، أى: صار هنيئا. وهنأنى الطعام يهنئني ويهنؤنى، ولا نظير له في المهموز هنأ وهناء. وهنئت الطعام، أى: تهنأت به، وكلوه هنيئا مريئا. (ع)
07
Q 69:25–29 · Vol. 4, pp. 603–604

Verses 25 to 29

The verses as the commentary quotes them
But as for he who is given his record in his left hand, he will say: Oh, I wish I had not been given my record (25) And had not known what my account is (26) Oh, I wish it had been the end! (27) My wealth has not availed me (28) My authority has perished from me (29)
وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِشِمالِهِ فَيَقُولُ يا لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُوتَ كِتابِيَهْ (25) وَلَمْ أَدْرِ ما حِسابِيَهْ (26) يا لَيْتَها كانَتِ الْقاضِيَةَ (27) ما أَغْنى عَنِّي مالِيَهْ (28) هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطانِيَهْ (29)
Vol. 4, p. 603
The pronoun in "Oh, I wish it" refers to the death: he says: "Would that the death which I died had been 'the end,'" that is, the severing
الضمير في يا لَيْتَها للموتة: يقول: يا ليت الموتة التي متها كانَتِ الْقاضِيَةَ أى القاطعة
Vol. 4, p. 604
of my affair, so that I would not have been resurrected after it and would not meet what I meet; or it refers to the condition, i.e., "would that this condition had been the death that finished me," because he saw that condition as more hideous and bitter than the bitterness and severity of death he had tasted, so he wished for death then. "What has availed": a negation, or a question of denial, i.e., what thing has availed me of the ease (wealth) I had? "My authority has perished from me": my kingship and my dominion over people, and I remain poor and humiliated. From Ibn 'Abbas: it was revealed about al-Aswad ibn 'Abd al-Asad. And from Fanakhusraw, nicknamed "al-'Adud": when he said, "'Adud al-Dawla and the son of its pillar … king of kings, conqueror of destiny" [1], he did not prosper after it and went mad, so that his tongue would utter nothing but this verse. Ibn 'Abbas said: "My argument has been lost to me." Its meaning: my argument by which I used to argue in the world has become void.
لأمرى، فلم أبعث بعدها، ولم ألق ما ألقى. أو للحالة، أى: ليت هذه الحالة كانت الموتة التي قضت علىّ، لأنه رأى تلك الحالة أبشع وأمر مما ذاقه من مرارة الموت وشدته، فتمناه عندها ما أَغْنى نفى أو استفهام على وجه الإنكار، أى: أىّ شيء أغنى عنى ما كان لي من اليسار هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطانِيَهْ ملكي وتسلطي على الناس، وبقيت فقيرا ذليلا. وعن ابن عباس: أنها نزلت في الأسود بن عبد الأشد. وعن فناخسرة الملقب بالعضد، أنه لما قال: عضد الدّولة وابن ركنها … ملك الأملاك غلّاب القدر «1» لم يفلح بعده وجنّ فكان لا ينطق لسانه إلا بهذه الآية. وقال ابن عباس: ضلت عنى حجتي. ومعناه: بطلت حجتي التي كنت أحتج بها في الدنيا.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 603

…. الخ» قال أحمد: تعليل القراءة باتباع المصحف عجيب مع أن المعتقد الحق أن القراآت السبع بتفاصيلها منقولة تواترا عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وعلى آله وسلم، فالذي أثبت الهاء في الوصل إنما أثبتها من التواتر عن قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: آيها كذلك قبل أن تكتب في المصحف، وما نفس هؤلاء إلا إدخال الاجتهاد في القراآت المستفيضة، واعتقاد أن فيها ما أخذ بالاختيار النظري وهذا خطأ لا ينبغي فتح بابه، فانه ذريعة إلى ما هو أكبر منه، ولقد جرت بيني وبين الشيخ أبى عمرو رحمه الله مفاوضة في قوله وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَيَخْشَ اللَّهَ وَيَتَّقْهِ على قراءة حفص، انتهت إلى أن ألزم الرد على من أثبت الهاء في الوصل في كلمات سورة الحاقة. لأنى حججته بإثبات القراء المشاهير لها كذلك، ففهمت من رده لذلك ما فهمه من كلام الزمخشري هاهنا ولم أقبله منه رحمه الله، فتراجع عنه، وكانت هذه المفاوضة بمكاتبة بيني وبينه، وهي آخر ما كتب من العلوم على ما أخبرنى به خاصته، وذلك صحيح لأنها كانت في أوائل مرضه رحمه الله، والله أعلم.

Vol. 4, p. 604
1. (1) . "Drinking the cup is nothing (sweet) except in the rain, and singing of girls at dawn — beautiful, plundering of minds, delicate, in the folds of the string, chilling the cup from its rising, pouring the cup — (they) surpass mankind. 'Adud al-Dawla and the son of its pillar, king of kings, conqueror of destiny." By al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Tusi; and it is said it is for 'Adud al-Dawla himself, saying: Drinking perfect-pleasure wine is nothing except in the rain and in the singing of slave-girls at dawn. "Ghaniyat": beautiful, dwelling in the eyes, virgins; "salibat": plunderers of the "nuha," plural of "nuhya," which is the mind; "na'imat": enjoying ease. "In the folds of the string" is connected to "singing." It is also transmitted "naghimat" with a dotted ghayn, i.e., making their voices beautiful amid the voice of the string, which is the cord stretched on the instrument of amusement. "Al-rah": wine. "'Adud al-Dawla" is an apposition of the relative object of "saqiyat." And "al-'adud" (the upper arm) is originally a metaphor for the one praised, for the state's strength is through him, like the arm for a human; and "al-rukn" (pillar) likewise a metaphor for his father, combining the idea of strengthening too, and this is nearer than likening the state at one time to a human and at another to a building, by way of implicit metaphor; but now they are two titles of the one praised and his father; and mentioning the pronoun and returning it to "al-dawla," although it is part of the name in both places, is to glance at the original, as in a metaphor. "Al-qadar": what God has decreed and judged. In describing the one praised as "conqueror of destiny" there is an element of impiety (the text reads "fujur al-nisa'", "the wickedness of women") that is not hidden; and for that reason it is narrated that he went mad and his tongue was restrained until he died. And from the Prophet ﷺ: "The most wrathful man against God on the Day of Resurrection, and the vilest of them, is a man who called himself King of Kings, and there is no king but God."
1. (1) . ليس شرب الكأس إلا في المطر
…. وغناء من جوار في سحر غانيات سالبات النهى
…. ناعمات في تضاعيف الوتر مبردات الكأس من مطلعها
…. ساقيات الكأس من فاق البشر عضد الدولة وابن ركنها
…. ملك الأملاك غلاب القدر الحسن بن على الطوسي. وقيل لعضد الدولة نفسه، يقول: ليس شرب الخمر الكامل اللذة إلا في حال المطر، وفي حال غناء الجواري في السحر، غانيات: جميلات مقيمات في العيون عذرات، سالبات: ناهبات للنهى: جمع نهية وهي العقل، ناعمات: أى متنعمات. وفي تضاعيف الوتر: متعلق بغناء. ويروى: ناغمات، بالمعجمة، أى: محسنات لأصواتهن في أثناء صوت الوتر، وهو الخيط المشدود في آلة اللهو. والراح: الخمر. وعضد الدولة: بدل من الموصول المفعول بساقيات. والعضد في الأصل: استعارة للممدوح لأن به قوتها. كالعضد للإنسان. والركن كذلك استعارة لأبيه يجامع التقوية أيضا، وهو أقرب من تشبيه الدولة بالإنسان تارة وبالبناء أخرى، على طريق المكنية، ولكنهما الآن لقبان للممدوح وأبيه، وذكر الضمير وإعادته على الدولة مع أنها جزء العلم في المحلين للمح الأصل كالاستعارة. والقدر: ما قدره الله وقضاه. وفي وصف ممدوحه بأنه غلاب القدر من فجور النساء ما لا يخفى، ولذلك روى أنه جن وحبس لسانه حتى مات: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أغيظ الناس رجلا على الله يوم القيامة وأخبثهم: رجل تسمى ملك الأملاك، ولا ملك إلا الله» .
08
Q 69:30–37 · Vol. 4, pp. 604–606

Verses 30 to 37

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Seize him and shackle him (30) Then into the Hellfire drive him (31) Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits insert him (32) Indeed, he did not believe in God, the Most Great (33) And did not encourage the feeding of the poor (34) So he has not here today any close friend (35) Nor any food except from pus (36) None will eat it except the sinners (37)
خُذُوهُ فَغُلُّوهُ (30) ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ (31) ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُها سَبْعُونَ ذِراعاً فَاسْلُكُوهُ (32) إِنَّهُ كانَ لا يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ (33) وَلا يَحُضُّ عَلى طَعامِ الْمِسْكِينِ (34) فَلَيْسَ لَهُ الْيَوْمَ هاهُنا حَمِيمٌ (35) وَلا طَعامٌ إِلاَّ مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ (36) لا يَأْكُلُهُ إِلاَّ الْخاطِؤُنَ (37)
Vol. 4, p. 604
"Then into the Hellfire drive him": then do not roast him except in the Hellfire, which is the greatest fire, because he was a ruler who exalted himself over people. It is said "sala al-nar" and "salahu al-nar." Inserting him in the chain: that it be wound around his body until its coils wrap
ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ ثم لا تصلوه إلا الجحيم، وهي النار العظمى، لأنه كان سلطانا يتعظم على الناس. يقال: صلى النار وصلاه النار. سلكه في السلسلة: أن تلوى على جسده حتى تلتف
Vol. 4, p. 605
upon him its folds, and he is between them pressed, constricted, unable to move; and making it seventy cubits is in order to describe its length, as He said, "If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times," meaning many times, because when it is long the pressing is more severe. The meaning of putting the chain before the insertion is like putting the Hellfire before the roasting: that is, "do not insert him except in this chain," as if it were more horrific than all other places of pressing in Hell. And the meaning of "then" (thumma) is to indicate the difference between shackling and roasting in the Hellfire, and between that and insertion in the chain, not a lapse of time. "Indeed, he": a rationale in the way of a fresh sentence, and that is more eloquent, as if it were said: "Why is he tortured with this severe torture?" and the answer was given thus. And in His words "and did not encourage the feeding of the poor" are two strong proofs of the gravity of the crime in depriving the poor: one, that He coordinated it with disbelief and made it its companion; the second, that He mentioned encouragement rather than the act, to make known that the one who neglects encouragement is at this rank, so what of one who neglects the act? And how fine is the poet's saying: "When guests alight, he is ill-tempered toward the household until their cauldrons rise" [1] — he means that he urged them to hospitality, hurried them, and quarreled with them [2]. From Abu al-Darda': that he used to urge his wife to increase the broth for the sake of the poor, and he used to say: "We removed half the chain by faith; shall we not remove the other half?" It is said: it means the prevention of the disbelievers; and their saying "Shall we feed one whom, if God willed, He would have fed?" And the meaning is on the giving of the poor's food. "Close friend" (hamim): a relative who defends him and grieves for him, because they shun him and flee from him,
عليه أثناؤها، وهو فيما بينها مرهق مضيق عليه لا يقدر على حركة، وجعلها سبعين ذراعا إرادة الوصف بالطول، كما قال: إن تستغفر لهم سبعين مرة، يريد: مرات كثيرة، لأنها إذا طالت كان الإرهاق أشد. والمعنى في تقديم السلسلة على السلك: مثله في تقديم الجحيم على النصلية. أى: لا تسلكوه إلا في هذه السلسلة، كأنها أفظع من سائر مواضع الإرهاق في الجحيم. ومعنى ثُمَّ الدلالة على تفاوت ما بين الغل والتصلية بالجحيم، وما بينها وبين السلك في السلسلة، لا على تراخى المدة إِنَّهُ تعليل على طريق الاستئناف، وهو أبلغ، كأنه قيل: ما له يعذب هذا العذاب الشديد؟ فأجيب بذلك. وفي قوله وَلا يَحُضُّ عَلى طَعامِ الْمِسْكِينِ دليلان قويان على عظم الجرم في حرمان المسكين، أحدهما: عطفه على الكفر، وجعله قرينة له. والثاني: ذكر الحض دون الفعل، ليعلم أنّ تارك الحض بهذه المنزلة، فكيف بتارك الفعل، وما أحسن قول القائل: إذا نزل الأضياف كان عذوّرا … على الحىّ حتّى تستقلّ مراجله «1» يريد حضهم على القرى واستعجلهم وتشاكس عليهم «2» . وعن أبى الدرداء أنه كان يحض امرأته على تكثير المرق لأجل المساكين، وكان يقول: خلعنا نصف السلسلة بالإيمان، أفلا نخلع نصفها الآخر؟ وقيل: هو منع الكفار. وقولهم: أَنُطْعِمُ مَنْ لَوْ يَشاءُ اللَّهُ أَطْعَمَهُ والمعنى على بذل طعام المسكين حَمِيمٌ قريب يدفع عنه ويحزن عليه، لأنهم يتحامونه ويفرون منه،
Vol. 4, p. 606
as in His words, "and no close friend will ask about a close friend." "Ghislin": the washings of the people of the Fire and what flows from their bodies of pus and blood — a "fi'lin" form from "al-ghasl" (washing). "The sinners" (al-khati'un): the wrongdoers, possessors of sins. And "khati'a al-rajul" when he intends sin deliberately [1]; and they are the polytheists, according to Ibn 'Abbas. It has also been read "al-khatiyun" with the hamza turned into ya', and "al-khatun" with it dropped. And from Ibn 'Abbas: "What is 'al-khatun'? All of us step (nakhtu)!" And Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali narrated from him: "What is 'al-khatun'? It is only 'al-khati'un.' What is 'al-sabun'? It is only 'al-sabi'un.'" It is also possible that what is meant are those who step beyond the truth into falsehood and transgress the limits of God.
كقوله وَلا يَسْئَلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيماً. والغسلين: غسالة أهل النار وما يسيل من أبدانهم من الصديد والدم، فعلين من الغسل الْخاطِؤُنَ الآثمون أصحاب الخطايا. وخطئ الرجل: إذا تعمد الذنب «1» ، وهم المشركون: عن ابن عباس: وقرئ: الخاطيون، بإبدال الهمزة ياء، والخاطون بطرحها. وعن ابن عباس: ما الخاطون؟ كلنا نخطو. وروى عنه أبو الأسود الدؤلي: ما الخاطون؟ إنما هو الخاطئون، ما الصابون؟ إنما هو الصابئون: ويجوز أن يراد: الذين يتخطون الحق إلى الباطل، ويتعدّون حدود الله.
Editor’s notes on these 3 pages
Vol. 4, p. 604
1. (1) . "Drinking the cup is nothing (sweet) except in the rain, and singing of girls at dawn — beautiful, plundering of minds, delicate, in the folds of the string, chilling the cup from its rising, pouring the cup — (they) surpass mankind. 'Adud al-Dawla and the son of its pillar, king of kings, conqueror of destiny." By al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Tusi; and it is said it is for 'Adud al-Dawla himself, saying: Drinking perfect-pleasure wine is nothing except in the rain and in the singing of slave-girls at dawn. "Ghaniyat": beautiful, dwelling in the eyes, virgins; "salibat": plunderers of the "nuha," plural of "nuhya," which is the mind; "na'imat": enjoying ease. "In the folds of the string" is connected to "singing." It is also transmitted "naghimat" with a dotted ghayn, i.e., making their voices beautiful amid the voice of the string, which is the cord stretched on the instrument of amusement. "Al-rah": wine. "'Adud al-Dawla" is an apposition of the relative object of "saqiyat." And "al-'adud" (the upper arm) is originally a metaphor for the one praised, for the state's strength is through him, like the arm for a human; and "al-rukn" (pillar) likewise a metaphor for his father, combining the idea of strengthening too, and this is nearer than likening the state at one time to a human and at another to a building, by way of implicit metaphor; but now they are two titles of the one praised and his father; and mentioning the pronoun and returning it to "al-dawla," although it is part of the name in both places, is to glance at the original, as in a metaphor. "Al-qadar": what God has decreed and judged. In describing the one praised as "conqueror of destiny" there is an element of impiety (the text reads "fujur al-nisa'", "the wickedness of women") that is not hidden; and for that reason it is narrated that he went mad and his tongue was restrained until he died. And from the Prophet ﷺ: "The most wrathful man against God on the Day of Resurrection, and the vilest of them, is a man who called himself King of Kings, and there is no king but God."
1. (1) . ليس شرب الكأس إلا في المطر
…. وغناء من جوار في سحر غانيات سالبات النهى
…. ناعمات في تضاعيف الوتر مبردات الكأس من مطلعها
…. ساقيات الكأس من فاق البشر عضد الدولة وابن ركنها
…. ملك الأملاك غلاب القدر الحسن بن على الطوسي. وقيل لعضد الدولة نفسه، يقول: ليس شرب الخمر الكامل اللذة إلا في حال المطر، وفي حال غناء الجواري في السحر، غانيات: جميلات مقيمات في العيون عذرات، سالبات: ناهبات للنهى: جمع نهية وهي العقل، ناعمات: أى متنعمات. وفي تضاعيف الوتر: متعلق بغناء. ويروى: ناغمات، بالمعجمة، أى: محسنات لأصواتهن في أثناء صوت الوتر، وهو الخيط المشدود في آلة اللهو. والراح: الخمر. وعضد الدولة: بدل من الموصول المفعول بساقيات. والعضد في الأصل: استعارة للممدوح لأن به قوتها. كالعضد للإنسان. والركن كذلك استعارة لأبيه يجامع التقوية أيضا، وهو أقرب من تشبيه الدولة بالإنسان تارة وبالبناء أخرى، على طريق المكنية، ولكنهما الآن لقبان للممدوح وأبيه، وذكر الضمير وإعادته على الدولة مع أنها جزء العلم في المحلين للمح الأصل كالاستعارة. والقدر: ما قدره الله وقضاه. وفي وصف ممدوحه بأنه غلاب القدر من فجور النساء ما لا يخفى، ولذلك روى أنه جن وحبس لسانه حتى مات: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أغيظ الناس رجلا على الله يوم القيامة وأخبثهم: رجل تسمى ملك الأملاك، ولا ملك إلا الله» .
Vol. 4, p. 605
1. (1) . "We left a youth whom hunger knew was its killer, when he settled among the people's saddles; a youth cut as the sword is cut, not shrinking, nor flabby in his chest or his thick veins. When guests alight, he is ill-tempered toward the household until their cauldrons rise." It is said that it is by al-'Ujayr al-Saluli; and it is said by Zaynab bint al-Tathriyya, lamenting her brother Yazid. "Al-laban al-ta'ir" and "al-khathir" have the same meaning. Hunger is likened to a human enemy of the people by implicit metaphor, and the affirmation of certainty for it is an imaginative element, as is its killing; and this is an exaggeration in describing Yazid's generosity, that he prevents hunger from entering the people's houses and reaching them, so that hunger as it were fears him and is certain that if it enters the people's houses Yazid will kill it. It is possible that the subject of "thawa" is the pronoun of Yazid, but the first is more eloquent, because it indicates that hunger did not enter upon the people because of its fear of Yazid. "Qudda": a verb in the passive; "qadda al-sayf": an absolute object, i.e., created in the shape of the sword in going through place and executing resolutions. "Al-mutada'il": the one who shrinks and humbles himself; "al-rahl" — like "ta'ab" — is flabbiness; "al-rahil" — like "hadhir" — is its adjective; and "al-labba" is made plural with regard to its surroundings. "Al-abajil": plural of "abjal," a thick vein in the thigh and the leg; and "a horse with 'wahn al-abajil'" is swift in running. "Al-'adhur" — with an unpointed 'ayn and doubled waw — is one of bad character and little patience in what he seeks, as if he needs to make excuses for his bad character. "Al-marajil": the large cooking pots. He says: we left in the battle a generous youth, bountiful and swift in hosting guests; when they alighted with him he was ill-tempered toward his family until their pots rose onto the hearthstones, and then his temper improved as it had been.
2. . His statement "and quarreled with them": in al-Sihah: "rajul shakis," i.e., difficult in character. ('A) [.....]
1. (1) . تركنا فتى قد أيقن الجوع أنه
…. إذا ما ثوى في أرحل القوم قاتله فتى قد قد السيف لا متضائل
…. ولا رهل لباته وأباجله إذا نزل الأضياف كان عذورا
…. على الحي حتى تستقل مراجله قيل: إنه للعجير السلولي. وقيل: لزينب بنت الطثرية ترثى أخاها يزيد. واللبن الطائر والخاثر: بمعنى. شبه الجوع بإنسان عدو للقوم على سبيل المكنية، وإثبات الإيقان له تخييل، وكذلك قتله، وهذا مبالغة في وصف يزيد بالكرم، وأنه مانع للجوع من دخوله بيوت القوم ولحوقه بهم، حتى كأن الجوع يخافه ويتيقن أنه إذا دخل بيوت القوم قتله يزيد. ويجوز أن فاعل ثوى: ضمير يزيد، لكن الأول أبلغ، لأنه يفيد أن الجوع لم يدخل على القوم لخوفه من يزيد، وقد: فعل مبنى للمجهول، وقد السيف: مفعول مطلق، أى خلق على شكل السيف في المضي في المكان وتنفيذ العزائم. والمتضائل المتضاعف المتخاشع، والرهل- كتعب-: الاسترخاء. والرهل- كحذر-: وصف منه، وجمع اللبة باعتبار ما حولها. والأباجل: جمع أبجل، وهو عرق غليظ في الفخذ والساق وفرس وهن الأباجل سريع الجري، والعذور- بالعين المهملة وتشديد الواو-: سيئ الخلق قليل الصبر عن مطلوبه، كأنه يحتاج إلى الاعتذار عن سوء خلقه. والمراجل: القدور العظام يقول: تركنا في المعركة فتى كريما جوادا سريعا في قرى الضيفان، إذا نزلوا به كان سيئ الخلق على أهله، حتى ترتفع قدوره الأثافى، فيحسن خلقه كما كان.
2. . قوله «وتشاكس عليهم» في الصحاح: رجل شكس، أى: صعب الخلق. (ع) [.....]
Vol. 4, p. 606
1. (1) . His statement "and khati'a al-rajul when he intends sin deliberately": in al-Sihah: al-Umawi said: "al-mukhti'" is one who wanted the right and ended up with other than it; and "al-khati'" is one who deliberately did what he ought not. ('A)
1. (1) . قوله «وخطئ الرجل إذا تعمد الذنب» في الصحاح: قال الأموى، المخطئ من أراد الصواب فصار إلى غيره. والخاطئ: من تعمد لما لا ينبغي. (ع)
09
Q 69:38–43 · Vol. 4, p. 606

Verses 38 to 43

The verses as the commentary quotes them
But no! I swear by what you see (38) And what you do not see (39) Indeed, it is the speech of a noble messenger (40) And it is not the speech of a poet; little do you believe (41) Nor the speech of a soothsayer; little do you remember (42) A revelation from the Lord of the worlds (43)
فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِما تُبْصِرُونَ (38) وَما لا تُبْصِرُونَ (39) إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ (40) وَما هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شاعِرٍ قَلِيلاً ما تُؤْمِنُونَ (41) وَلا بِقَوْلِ كاهِنٍ قَلِيلاً ما تَذَكَّرُونَ (42) تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ (43)
Vol. 4, p. 606
It is an oath by all things, in totality and encompassment, because they do not fall outside two divisions: seen and unseen. It is also said: this world and the Hereafter, bodies and spirits, humans and jinn, creation and the Creator, the outward and inward blessings. "Indeed, this Qur'an is the speech of a noble messenger," i.e., he says it and speaks it by way of messengership from God. "And it is not the speech of a poet," nor of a soothsayer, as you claim. And "little" is in the sense of "none": that is, you do not believe and do not remember at all. The meaning: how disbelieving you are and how heedless you are! "A revelation": it is a revelation, as an explanation that it is the speech of a messenger upon whom it was revealed "from the Lord of the worlds." Abu al-Sammal read "tanzilan," i.e., "revealed (as) a revelation." It is also said that "the noble messenger" is Gabriel ﷺ while His words "and it is not the speech of a poet" are proof that it is Muhammad ﷺ because the meaning is on establishing that he is a messenger, neither poet nor soothsayer.
هو إقسام بالأشياء كلها على الشمول والإحاطة، لأنها لا تخرج من قسمين: مبصر وغير مبصر. وقيل: الدنيا والآخرة، والأجسام والأرواح، والإنس والجنّ، والخلق والخالق، والنعم الظاهرة والباطنة، إن هذا القرآن لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ أى يقوله ويتكلم به على وجه الرسالة من عند الله وَما هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شاعِرٍ ولا كاهن كما تدعون والقلة في معنى العدم. أى: لا تؤمنون ولا تذكرون ألبتة. والمعنى: ما أكفركم وما أغفلكم تَنْزِيلٌ هو تنزيل، بيانا لأنه قول رسول نزل عليه مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ وقرأ أبو السمال: تنزيلا، أى: نزل تنزيلا. وقيل «الرسول الكريم» جبريل عليه السلام، وقوله وَما هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شاعِرٍ دليل على أنه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنّ المعنى على إثبات أنه رسول، لا شاعر ولا كاهن.

Q 69:44–52 · Vol. 4, pp. 606–607

Verses 44 to 52

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And if he had made up about Us some sayings (44) We would have seized him by the right hand (45) Then We would have cut from him the aorta (46) And there is not one of you who could have shielded (him) from it (47) And indeed, it is a reminder for the righteous (48) And indeed, We know that among you are deniers (49) And indeed, it is a regret upon the disbelievers (50) And indeed, it is the certain truth (51) So exalt the name of your Lord, the Most Great (52)
وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيْنا بَعْضَ الْأَقاوِيلِ (44) لَأَخَذْنا مِنْهُ بِالْيَمِينِ (45) ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنا مِنْهُ الْوَتِينَ (46) فَما مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حاجِزِينَ (47) وَإِنَّهُ لَتَذْكِرَةٌ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ (48) وَإِنَّا لَنَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مِنْكُمْ مُكَذِّبِينَ (49) وَإِنَّهُ لَحَسْرَةٌ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ (50) وَإِنَّهُ لَحَقُّ الْيَقِينِ (51) فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ (52)
Vol. 4, p. 607
"Al-taqawwul" is the fabrication of speech [1], as if there were affectation on the part of the fabricator. The fabricated sayings were called "aqawil" to belittle and demean them, as in your saying "al-a'ajib" and "al-adahik," as if they were plurals of the "uf'ula" form from "al-qawl." The meaning: if he had claimed against Us something We had not said, We would have killed him in captivity (sabran), as kings do to one who lies about them, hastening wrath and vengeance; so He pictured the killing by captivity in its form to make it more terrifying — which is that he is seized by the hand and his neck is struck. He specified the right rather than the left because the executioner, when he wants to deliver the blow to the nape of his neck, takes him by his left, and when he wants to deliver it to his throat and confront him with the sword — which is harder on the one being killed since he sees the sword — takes him by his right. The meaning of "We would have seized him by the right hand" is "We would have seized his right hand," just as "We would have cut from him the aorta" is "We would have cut his aorta," and this is clear. "Al-watin": the artery of the heart, which is the jugular cord; if it is cut, its owner dies. It has also been read "wa-law taqawwala" in the passive. "Shielding" (hajizin) was said in describing "ahad," because it is in the sense of a group, and it is a noun that occurs in general negation, the singular and plural, masculine and feminine being equal in it. From it is His saying, Exalted is He, "We make no distinction between any of His messengers," "you are not like any (ahad) of the women." And the pronoun in "from him" refers to the killing, i.e., none of you could shield him from that or ward it off from him; or to the Messenger of God, i.e., you cannot shield the killer from him and stand between them. The address is to the people, and likewise in His words, Exalted is He, "And indeed, We know that among you are deniers," which is a threat against denial. It is also said that the address is to the Muslims, and the meaning is that among them are people who will disbelieve in the Qur'an. "And indeed it": the pronoun refers to the Qur'an "is a regret upon the disbelievers" in it who deny it, when they see the reward of those who believe in it; or it refers to the denial. "And indeed it is the certain truth": that the Qur'an is certainty, the very truth of certainty, as in your saying "he is the scholar, true scholar, the utmost scholar." The meaning: the very essence of certainty and pure certainty. "So exalt" God by mentioning His great name, which is His saying "Glory be to God," and worship Him in gratitude for what He has qualified you for by His revelation to you. From the Messenger of God ﷺ: "Whoever recites Surah al-Haqqah, God will reckon with him an easy reckoning" [2].
التقوّل: افتعال القول «1» ، كأن فيه تكلفا من المفتعل. وسمى الأقوال المتقولة «أقاويل» تصغيرا بها وتحقيرا، كقولك: الأعاجيب والأضاحيك، كأنها جمع أفعولة من القول. والمعنى: ولو ادعى علينا شيئا لم نقله لقتلناه صبرا، كما يفعل الملوك بمن يتكذب عليهم معاجلة بالسخط والانتقام، فصوّر قتل الصبر بصورته ليكون أهول: وهو أن يؤخذ بيده وتضرب رقبته. وخص اليمين عن اليسار لأن القتال إذا أراد أن يوقع الضرب في قفاه أخذ بيساره، وإذا أراد أن يوقعه في جيده وأن يكفحه بالسيف، وهو أشد على المصبور لنظره إلى السيف أخذ بيمينه. ومعنى لَأَخَذْنا مِنْهُ بِالْيَمِينِ لأخذنا بيمينه، كما أن قوله لَقَطَعْنا مِنْهُ الْوَتِينَ لقطعنا وتينه، وهذا بين. والوتين: نياط القلب وهو حبل الوريد: إذا قطع مات صاحبه. وقرئ: ولو تقول على البناء للمفعول. قيل حاجِزِينَ في وصف أحد، لأنه في معنى الجماعة، وهو اسم يقع في النفي العام مستويا فيه الواحد والجمع والمذكر والمؤنث. ومنه قوله تعالى لا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ، لَسْتُنَّ كَأَحَدٍ مِنَ النِّساءِ والضمير في عنه للقتل، أى: لا يقدر أحد منكم أن يحجزه عن ذلك ويدفعه عنه. أو لرسول الله، أى: لا تقدرون أن تحجزوا عنه القاتل وتحولوا بينه وبينه، والخطاب للناس، وكذلك في قوله تعالى وَإِنَّا لَنَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مِنْكُمْ مُكَذِّبِينَ وهو إيعاد على التكذيب. وقيل الخطاب للمسلمين. والمعنى: أن منهم ناسا سيكفرون بالقرآن وَإِنَّهُ الضمير للقرآن لَحَسْرَةٌ على الكافرين به المكذبين له إذا رأوا ثواب المصدقين به. أو للتكذيب، وأن القرآن اليقين حق اليقين، كقولك: هو العالم حق العالم، وجدّ العالم. والمعنى: لعين اليقين، ومحض اليقين فَسَبِّحْ الله بذكر اسمه العظيم وهو قوله: سبحان الله، واعبده شكرا على ما أهلك له من إيحائه إليك. عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من قرأ سورة الحاقة حاسبه الله حسابا يسيرا» «2» .
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 606
1. (1) . His statement "and khati'a al-rajul when he intends sin deliberately": in al-Sihah: al-Umawi said: "al-mukhti'" is one who wanted the right and ended up with other than it; and "al-khati'" is one who deliberately did what he ought not. ('A)
1. (1) . قوله «وخطئ الرجل إذا تعمد الذنب» في الصحاح: قال الأموى، المخطئ من أراد الصواب فصار إلى غيره. والخاطئ: من تعمد لما لا ينبغي. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 607
1. (1) . Mahmud said: "Al-taqawwul: ifti'al from al-qawl, because it contains affectation … etc." Ahmad said: Building "uq'ula" from "al-qawl," which is a weak (hollow) root, as you see, is hidden from the rules of morphology. It is possible that "al-aqawil" is a plural of a plural, like "al-ana'im," a plural of "aqwal" and "an'am," and that is the apparent sense, and God knows best.
2. . Narrated by al-Tha'labi, al-Wahidi and Ibn Mardawayh with the chain to Ubayy ibn Ka'b.
1. (1) . قال محمود: «التقول: افتعال من القول، لأن فيه تكلفا
…. الخ» قال أحمد: وبناء أقعولة من القول، وهو معتل، كما ترى غيب عن القياس التصريفى. ويحتمل أن تكون الأقاويل جمع الجمع، كالأناعيم: جمع أقوال وأنعام، وهو الظاهر، والله أعلم.
2. . أخرجه الثعلبي والواحدي وابن مردويه بالسند إلى أبى بن كعب.
